conservation.help_by: Use reef-safe sunscreen; choose operators that don’t touch or kick coral.
conservation.caution_against: Never stand on, break, or collect living coral.

life_info.eating: Energy from symbiotic algae plus night zooplankton. Polyps open more at night to snag tiny prey.
life_info.mating: Mass spawning events timed to lunar cycles.
life_info.habitat: Back-reef and lagoon patches with branching thickets. Nursery structure for juvenile reef fish.

fun_facts: Looks like underwater deer antlers in dense gardens.
Restoration nurseries grow fragments to replant reefs.

conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Algae scraped from rock and dead coral. Beak bites leave pale scrapes; sand in their waste helps build beaches.
life_info.mating: Complex sex change: some females become bright terminal-phase males.
life_info.habitat: Seagrass beds and coral reefs; sleeps in a mucus cocoon by night. Daytime grazing groups; night solo sleepers in slimy sleeping bags.

fun_facts: Much soft white beach sand started as parrotfish poop — glamorous, right?
The ‘stoplight’ name nods to red, yellow, and green color phases.
